paragraphs: Dimonoff sells smart street lighting control, connecting street and commercial lighting to a single platform so teams can monitor every fixture in real time. The site dates its work in smart street lighting control back to 2006.

A controller fits a NEMA or Zhaga socket on any LED fixture, from any manufacturer, and dims over 0-10V or DALI. The nodes network over Wi-SUN, RF mesh or LTE-M, and keep running their schedule if the link drops. In the office, one interface holds groups, schedules, dimming profiles, faults and reports, and pushes work orders into the asset system a city already runs. The platform also manages nodes from third-party manufacturers, so hardware from a previous supplier does not have to be scrapped. One part number covers supply voltages from 110 to 480 Vac nominal at 50/60 Hz. Node firmware is updated over the air rather than by a crew in a truck.

Networks already running on the platform account for more than 219,500 connected endpoints, by the company's count. Dimonoff states that all of its hardware and software is designed, developed, manufactured and supported in North America. The support FAQ names Groupe Vectanor as the parent company and says it joined the Wi-SUN Alliance as a Contributing Member in April 2026.
